blocks.text: PAGE 1 — Understand HTML Text and Headings

Welcome to Lesson 2: HTML Text and Headings. This lesson follows the course dashboard topic “HTML Text and Headings”. The goal is to headings, paragraphs, strong text, emphasis, lists and other text elements.. Focus on understanding when this technique is useful, what assumptions it makes, and how you can check that it is working.

HTML text elements communicate structure and meaning, not just visual size. Use heading levels in a logical hierarchy, paragraphs for blocks of prose, and emphasis elements according to meaning rather than choosing a tag only because of its default appearance.

Practice direction: Open Home → Menu → Practical/Practice → select HTML. Paste this snippet into the matching web/React editor, run or preview it, and compare what happens. Then change one value or element and run it again so you can observe the effect. If this course is not available in the in-app runner, use a suitable compiler or interpreter for the language.

blocks.question: A page uses an h1, then jumps to h4 because h4 looks smaller. What should guide heading levels?
options: The page’s logical section hierarchy; CSS can control appearance.
blocks.explanation: Heading levels communicate document structure; styling should not determine semantic order.
blocks.hint: Identify the requirement in the scenario, eliminate choices that ignore it, and choose the option that preserves correctness and maintainability.
blocks.correctFeedback: Correct. Heading levels communicate document structure; styling should not determine semantic order.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Review the requirement again. Heading levels communicate document structure; styling should not determine semantic order.

blocks.question: A phrase must be marked as important, not merely bold-looking. Which approach is best?
options: Use a meaningful element such as strong when its meaning is importance.
Put it in a div with no context.
blocks.explanation: Semantic elements communicate meaning while CSS controls appearance.
blocks.hint: Identify the requirement in the scenario, eliminate choices that ignore it, and choose the option that preserves correctness and maintainability.
blocks.correctFeedback: Correct. Semantic elements communicate meaning while CSS controls appearance.

blocks.text: Lists are useful when items belong together, while headings divide content into navigable sections. A page that has clear structure is easier to skim, style, maintain, and interpret with assistive technology.

blocks.question: A program repeatedly looks up a learner by a unique email address. Which structure is a natural fit?
options: A map/dictionary keyed by email, with suitable uniqueness handling.
A random number with no mapping.
A paragraph of comma-separated values that is never parsed.
A loop that guesses the correct person.
blocks.explanation: Key-value structures express lookup by identifier more directly than repeatedly scanning unrelated data.
blocks.hint: Identify the requirement in the scenario, eliminate choices that ignore it, and choose the option that preserves correctness and maintainability.
blocks.correctFeedback: Correct. Key-value structures express lookup by identifier more directly than repeatedly scanning unrelated data.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Review the requirement again. Key-value structures express lookup by identifier more directly than repeatedly scanning unrelated data.
